name: Netting a buy and sell tape
brief:
An internal crossing engine reads a tape of orders: a positive number is a buy of that many lots, a negative one a sell. Each sell nets first against the newest buy still resting, then the next newest, until it is used up or no buy is left. A sell with nothing left to net against rests too, and later buys never reach it. Each resting order stays a separate entry.

Write `net_tape(orders)`, which returns what still rests after the whole tape, oldest first.

Example. For `[5, 3, -4, 2, -9]`, the -4 uses all 3 and 1 of the 5, leaving `[4]`. Then 2 rests, and -9 uses the 2 and the 4 and rests as -3. The answer is `[-3]`.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 200{,}000$ orders, each a non-zero whole number between $-10^9$ and $10^9$.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Rebuilding the list after each sell is too slow.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep the resting orders on a stack. For a sell, while the top is a buy and the sell is not used up, take from the top. Push whatever is left of the sell.

examples.note: The sells eat the newest buys first; 3 lots of the last sell find nothing and rest.
The sell comes first and the later buy never reaches it.

how: Submit runs 14 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Only the newest resting buy can be hit next, which is the top of a stack.
A sell may use several buys. It rests only once every buy is gone, so later buys stack above it and never reach it.
Each order is pushed once and popped at most once, so the work is $O(n)$.

planted.slip: It rebuilds the resting list with a slice each time a buy is used up or trimmed, so every sell copies the whole list and the total is quadratic.
